decisions.question: Applied signature policy for Extract
candidates: A — hard refuse any source carrying an applied signature
B — allow the unsigned derivative, but remove the signature widget and its appearance stream
C — allow, with a persistent artifact-level indication that this is an unsigned derivative
decisions.measured: The cryptographic signature is removed and the appearance is not. After a legacy extract the AcroForm is absent, no signature field remains, and one widget survives carrying its /AP. Rendering the signature rectangle gives 4,325 non-white pixels out of 24,300 in the source and 4,325 out of 24,300 in the extract — pixel for pixel identical. A reader opening the derived file sees a signed-looking block on a document that carries no signature.
decisions.adopted: B — allow the unsigned derivative, removing the signature widget and its appearance stream; a persistent artifact-level indication stays DEFER
decisions.why: The previous recommendation allowed the unsigned derivative without saying anything about the appearance, which the measurement now shows is the part the reader actually sees. Removing the widget and its /AP makes the derived document honestly unsigned. C is a reasonable addition to B rather than an alternative to it; A remains correct for anyone who does not want derived copies of signed documents at all.
defer: what a persistent artifact-level indication should be (C) — visible watermark, metadata, or both

decisions.question: Applied signature policy for Merge
candidates: A — refuse any source carrying an applied signature
B — permit with explicit confirmation
decisions.measured: Merging a signed source produced a 5-page ordinary file with no mention of the signature. The appearance finding in M6-H1 applies here too, and is worse: the signed document's appearance now sits among other people's content.
decisions.adopted: A — refuse any Merge source carrying an applied signature
decisions.why: Unchanged by the new evidence, and strengthened by it. The asymmetry with M6-H1 is deliberate: an extract is openly a derivative of one document, a merge is a new document that would carry another's signature block.

decisions.question: Internal destinations pointing at pages excluded from an Extract
candidates: E1 — refuse the selected set, naming the pages that would break
E2 — keep the set, remove or retarget the link, report the loss
E3 — drop the link silently (not recommended)
decisions.measured: Today is none of these. Measured per shape: a destination to a SELECTED page still produces an orphan copy and lands outside the page tree (dest-direct-2p with both pages kept: 2 in tree, 1 orphan, 0 destinations landing in the document); the same holds for /A /GoTo /D. Cyclic destinations produce 2 orphans from a one-page selection. An article bead reaches another page with no annotation involved at all. The E2 prototype produces 0 orphan pages in all ten cases, every surviving destination lands in the output page tree, and every removed one is reported; E1 refuses before copying anything.
decisions.recommended: E2 as the default, E1 available as a stricter setting, and the invariant below adopted as a production contract
decisions.adopted: E2 as the default and E1 as a stricter setting, with the invariant adopted as a production contract: orphanPageCount === 0 and every surviving internal destination targets the output page tree
decisions.invariant: every indirect /Page object in an Extract artifact is a member of its output page tree (orphanPageCount === 0), and every surviving internal destination targets a page of that tree
decisions.why: E0 — what ships today — is worse than E3: it keeps a link that navigates nowhere a reader can reach AND ships the content of pages the user did not select. The invariant is checkable after serialization, which is where it is checked in the gate.

decisions.question: Outlines, named destinations and page labels
candidates: reconstruct for kept pages
declare dropped and name the loss
decisions.measured: All three are dropped by both operations today, even when every page is extracted. Named destinations ARE reconstructable: the E2 prototype rebuilds the entries whose target survives and reports the rest — with both pages of dest-named-2p kept, 4 destinations land in the document and nothing is lost; keeping only page 1, the surviving entry is rebuilt and 2 losses are reported by name. Outlines and page labels were NOT prototyped.
decisions.recommended: reconstruct named destinations (proven); treat outlines and page labels as reconstructable in principle but unproven here
decisions.adopted: reconstruct named destinations only; outlines and page labels DEFER
decisions.why: Saying 'reconstruct' for all three would claim evidence that exists for one of them. Page labels are arithmetic on /Nums and outlines are a tree walk, so neither looks hard — but neither has been shown to work, and the difference between those two statements is the point of this document.
defer: outline reconstruction, including hierarchies deeper than one level
page-label range arithmetic across a non-contiguous selection

decisions.question: Optional content — /OCProperties
candidates: carry the configuration for groups the kept pages reference, refusing anything outside the handled envelope
refuse every document carrying optional content
drop and confirm the visibility change
decisions.measured: Today's drop is not clean: before {ocProperties: true, pageOptionalContentProperties: true}, after {false, true} — the page's marked content still names a group the document no longer configures, so a viewer shows its own default rather than the author's. Thirteen documents now carry and match their source after the artifact is reopened, on group count, group names, ON, OFF, /D /Name, /BaseState, /D /Order structure and page /Properties resolution, all equal in every one. Eight for the group mapping: ocproperties (1 carried, 1 on), ocg-multiple (2 carried, 1 on, 1 off), ocg-two-pages-opposite (2 carried, on [M6-OCG-A], off [M6-OCG-B]), ocg-shared-across-pages (1 carried, referenced from both pages), ocg-reordered-properties (2 carried, keys written in opposite order on each page), ocg-many-pages (3 carried over 3 pages, 2 on, 1 off, one shared), ocg-d-name (/D /Name reproduced), ocg-basestate-on (/BaseState /ON reproduced). Five for the order structure: ocg-order-flat, ocg-order-nested, ocg-order-labeled-nested, ocg-order-empty (stays empty) and ocg-order-absent (stays absent). The two-page opposite-state pairing is the one an earlier positional mapping could invert. Refused with UNSUPPORTED_OPTIONAL_CONTENT: ocmd, ocmd-nested, ocg-basestate-off, ocg-order-malformed, ocg-configs, annot-oc, xobject-oc, malformed-ocproperties, ocg-order-invalid-top-label, ocg-order-invalid-mid-label, ocg-order-unused-group, ocg-missing-ocgs, ocg-missing-d, ocg-dangling-ocgs-ref, ocg-nested-form-xobject, ocg-form-properties, ocg-annotation-appearance-properties, ocg-pattern-properties, ocg-type3-properties, resource-cycle and resource-depth-exceeded. The fourteen supported fixtures still read as carryable with the resource-graph walker in place. ocg-extgstate-smask, a group behind a soft mask /G, extracted READY until B1 opened that path; it is refused now, together with smask-dangling-g, smask-malformed, smask-g-not-form, smask-shared-g and smask-depth-exceeded, while smask-clean and smask-none still carry.

envelope.carried: the page's own /Resources /Properties entries resolving to plain /OCG dictionaries, with a /D whose keys are within Order, ON, OFF, Name, BaseState — and which are reproduced in the artifact, not merely accepted at the door
envelope.refused: /OCMD in any form, a /VE visibility expression, a /BaseState other than /ON, any other /D key, an /Order entry that is neither a group, a nested array nor a text label, an /Order text label anywhere but the first element of a nested array, an /Order naming a group no kept page uses, any /Properties entry that is neither /OCG nor /OCMD, /OCProperties /Configs, an annotation carrying /OC, an XObject carrying /OC at any depth the walker reaches, an /OCProperties that cannot be read, an /OCProperties without /OCGs or without /D, an /OCGs entry that does not resolve or is not a group, any /Properties entry below the page's own resources — in a form XObject, an annotation appearance stream, a tiling pattern, a Type 3 font or a soft mask /G — a soft mask that cannot be read or is neither /None nor a dictionary, a soft mask /G that is missing, dangling or not a form XObject stream, and a resource graph deeper than 24 scopes

decisions.detectionEnvelope: A contract that refuses everything outside the handled shapes is only true if the unhandled shapes can be found. The detector has been widened three times, each time with a fixture per shape; the third is B1, described below. First, four attachment points that were invisible: /OCProperties /Configs (ocg-configs), an annotation's /OC (annot-oc), an XObject's /OC (xobject-oc) and an /OCProperties that cannot be walked (malformed-ocproperties). Second, the resource graph below the page, which a page-level scan never opened: a form XObject two levels down carrying /OC (ocg-nested-form-xobject), a form XObject's own /Resources /Properties (ocg-form-properties), an annotation appearance stream's own /Resources /Properties (ocg-annotation-appearance-properties), a tiling pattern's (ocg-pattern-properties) and a Type 3 font's (ocg-type3-properties). Required keys fail closed: a missing /OCGs (ocg-missing-ocgs) or /D (ocg-missing-d) is refused rather than read as an empty default, and an /OCGs entry pointing at an object that does not exist (ocg-dangling-ocgs-ref) is refused rather than read as a value. The walk is bounded: a visited set keyed on indirect references ends a cycle and counts a shared object once (resource-cycle — the group behind the cycle is reported exactly once and the depth bound is never reached), and a graph deeper than 24 scopes is refused rather than reported as clean (resource-depth-exceeded). Walked: /Annots and their /AP streams, /XObject, /Pattern, Type 3 /Font, /ExtGState as far as a soft mask /G, and /Properties below the page's own scope. Not walked: /ColorSpace and /Shading, which open no content stream. /ExtGState was on that list until B1: a soft mask /G is a form XObject with resources of its own, and ocg-extgstate-smask extracted READY with a group behind it. The walker now opens it through the same walk, visited set and depth bound — smask-shared-g reports the group behind a shared /G once, and smask-depth-exceeded is refused at the bound; a clean mask and /SMask /None are not refused (smask-clean, smask-none), and an unreadable mask or a dangling or non-form /G is (smask-malformed, smask-dangling-g, smask-g-not-form). Followed by the walker but exercised by no fixture: /AP state dictionaries, image XObjects below the page, and /CharProcs streams carrying their own /Resources. Support was not widened by any of this: the refusals became real.
decisions.orderRule: /Order is mapped recursively rather than flattened: a group reference becomes the mapped output reference, a nested array becomes a nested array, an absent /Order stays absent and an empty one stays empty. A text label is reproduced only where this research has shown it can be — as the first element of a nested array, titling a section. A label at the top level (ocg-order-invalid-top-label) or part-way through a nested array (ocg-order-invalid-mid-label) is refused rather than carried on the strength of being a string, and an /Order naming a group no kept page uses (ocg-order-unused-group) is refused rather than silently dropped. Proven on five carried shapes — flat, empty, absent, nested, and nested opening with a label — each compared as a structure after reopening the artifact, not as a set of groups. An earlier version collected only the references it found at any depth and rewrote a flat array, so nesting and labels were silently lost, an empty /Order was filled in and an absent one was invented; the comparison did not notice because it compared the set.
decisions.mapping: structural: (selected source page + /Properties key + source OCG ref) to (output page + same key + output OCG ref), with the resulting output refs deduplicated. Positions are never used, so a page whose keys are written in a different order, or a group referenced from two pages, still resolves. An earlier version paired by position and reset its source cursor on every output page: one kept page worked, two could swap ON for OFF.
decisions.detector: catalog /OCProperties present, or optional content found by walking each kept page's resource graph — /Annots and their /AP streams, /XObject, /Pattern, Type 3 /Font and soft mask /G scopes, recursively — with a visited set and a depth bound of 24; an unresolvable reference is a refusal, not an absence
decisions.recommended: carry within the envelope above; typed refusal outside it
decisions.adopted: carry only the proven direct-/OCG envelope; typed refusal outside it; closing the /ExtGState /SMask /G path is mandatory before implementation (B1)
decisions.implementationBlocker: B1 — CLOSED on 2026-09-15. The /ExtGState /SMask /G path, which the walker did not open at adoption, had to be closed before implementation; it was closed the recommended way, by walking the soft-mask form's resources under the existing fail-closed contract (ocg-extgstate-smask READY before, REFUSED after). READY with that path unwalked stays forbidden.
decisions.why: Carrying is proven for the direct-/OCG case and the refusal is proven for /OCMD, so neither half is asserted. An /OCMD decides visibility from a set of groups and optionally a nested boolean expression; carrying a subset of that evaluation would silently change what the reader sees, which is the failure this decision exists to prevent.
defer: /OCMD, with or without a /VE visibility expression — refused for now, not designed
/BaseState /OFF and /Unchanged
usage application dictionaries, /RBGroups and /Locked, which fall outside the handled /D keys

decisions.question: Document JavaScript and /OpenAction
candidates: refuse any JavaScript-bearing source
sanitize: remove and prove by readback
carry
decisions.measured: Seven sites, each with its own fixture, each found by the scanner in the source and absent from the sanitized output measured by reopening it: /Names /JavaScript, /OpenAction as a JavaScript action, annotation /A, annotation /AA, page /AA, field /AA, and JavaScript behind a /Next. Total remaining after readback across all seven: 0. A document with no JavaScript scans 0 and completes. An action reachable by two routes through the same holder is counted once — 1 action from 2 visits. Five /Next shapes then measured separately, all reaching 0 remaining: a dictionary, an array, an array whose second element is JavaScript, JavaScript two links down a nested chain, and one action referenced from two annotations (2 sites, 2 removed — different holders, so two references rather than one). A cyclic action graph is refused with UNSCANNABLE_ACTIONS rather than passed.
decisions.arrayRule: an array's meaning is decided by the key holding it: a destination under /OpenAction, /Dest or /D; a list of actions under /Next, every element of which is walked. An earlier version treated every array as a destination and stopped, so JavaScript inside a /Next array was never visited and the document passed.
decisions.boundedBy: MAX_ACTION_DEPTH 32, with a per-chain cycle set; a chain deeper than the bound, a cycle, or an action dictionary that cannot be read makes the document UNSCANNABLE_ACTIONS rather than a quiet pass
decisions.mechanismNote: Two of the seven sites reach zero because copyPages never copies catalog-level structure, not because the sanitizer removed them. Recorded per site rather than summarised, so a future change that started copying /Names would not silently move a row from one column to the other.
decisions.artifactWideRule: The contract is two counts at zero, not one: what a reader can reach, and what the object table holds. Deleting the key that points at an action detaches it; it does not delete the object, and pdf-lib writes everything registered in the context whether or not anything points at it — the same mechanism that leaves orphaned pages behind after a copyPages. Measured: five of seven JavaScript cases put an action into the artifact's object table at all (annotation /A, annotation /AA, /Next, a doubly-nested /Next, and one indirect action referenced twice — 1 object each after the copy); the other two hold the action as a direct dictionary inside the annotation, so it never becomes a separate object. Every JavaScript action dictionary is now scrubbed of its entries and deleted from the table, and the artifact-wide count after reopening is 0 in all seven. Before this, 'no reachable JavaScript' was a true sentence about a file that still carried the script.
decisions.recommended: sanitize and prove by readback, refusing any document the scanner cannot finish inspecting; /OpenAction whose action is a page destination stays with M6-H5
decisions.adopted: sanitize and prove by readback: reachable JavaScript count === 0 AND artifact-wide indirect JavaScript action count === 0; UNSCANNABLE_ACTIONS when the scan cannot finish
decisions.why: Carrying document JavaScript into a derived document is a security decision nobody asked for, and refusing on mere presence would block documents where the script is incidental. What makes sanitization recommendable rather than hopeful is the readback count, and what makes it safe is that an uninspectable document is refused.
defer: action types beyond JavaScript — /Launch, /ImportData and friends are not part of this envelope

decisions.question: Embedded files and attachments
candidates: carry
remove with explicit confirmation
refuse
decisions.measured: Dropped silently by both operations. pdf-lib has a write path for embedding files but no read path for copying a source's.
decisions.detector: catalog /Names /EmbeddedFiles present, or any /Filespec with an /EF
decisions.recommended: remove with explicit confirmation for Extract; carry for Merge is DEFER
decisions.adopted: Extract: remove with explicit confirmation naming the files; Merge: carrying attachments is DEFER
decisions.why: An attachment belongs to the document, not to a page, so an extract of two pages has no principled claim to it — but losing one silently is the behaviour being corrected. The confirmation names the files being dropped.
defer: carrying attachments through a Merge, where the union is at least well defined

decisions.question: Merge intake — all-or-nothing or explicit partial
candidates: all-or-nothing
explicit partial with every omission named
decisions.measured: Today a non-PDF is skipped by a bare continue and a failed load is caught and logged to the console; the file never appears in the list. broken-pagetree and malformed-acroform both LOAD cleanly, so intake cannot be 'whatever the loader accepts'.
decisions.recommended: explicit partial, with a per-input typed result and every omission named in the UI
decisions.adopted: explicit partial intake, with a per-input typed result and every omitted source shown in the UI
decisions.why: Matches M5's adopted B2 batch shape. The page tree must be walked during intake, because two hostile fixtures load without complaint.

decisions.question: Memory and output ceilings
candidates: reuse M5's 512 MiB / 1 GiB / 2 GiB presets and MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES 268435456
derive M6-specific ceilings
adopt the output ceiling now and defer the memory budget to a sub-spike
decisions.measured: The dominant memory term — what a parsed pdf-lib document and its copied object graph weigh — is a function of document structure rather than byte length, and is UNKNOWN. The output ceiling needs no model: admitted at 3,462 B, refused at 3,461 B, at a boundary taken from a real artifact. No such check exists today.
decisions.recommended: adopt an actual-artifact output ceiling now, sharing M5's constant; do NOT adopt a memory preset until an Object-Graph Memory Sub-Spike closes the UNKNOWN
decisions.adopted: adopt an actual-artifact output ceiling; memory presets NOT ADOPTABLE; the Object-Graph Memory Sub-Spike is mandatory before implementation (B2)
decisions.implementationBlocker: B2 — CLOSED on 2026-09-15 as PARTIALLY BOUNDABLE. The Object-Graph Memory Sub-Spike found the copy and the plain save countable before they happen, the load not boundable with pdf-lib 1.17.1, and no memory preset adoptable; the load boundary it could not close is proposed as B3. B3 — accepted by the Human on 2026-09-15 and CLOSED by research on 2026-09-16 as A: a pre-parse boundary refuses, before load, what pdf-lib's load would expand past structural caps. The Human adopted that conclusion and the production load architecture on 2026-09-16 (loadBoundaryDecisions). B4 — product load policy and real-drawing compatibility — is OPEN, and blocks Ready, release and production enablement, not implementation.

hardStructuralTerms: objects the copy registers, copier map entries, raw stream bytes the copy duplicates, the largest stream, unselected pages reached — after load, before copy (EXACT; equal to the real copy in 15 shapes)
Merge output growth per source — before that source is copied (EXACT; equal in 2 merges)
plain-writer output length — before its buffer is allocated (EXACT; equal in 3 cases)
unknownTerms: the load: every object parsed eagerly, every object and xref stream inflated with no cap; input bytes do not bound it
heap bytes per object, per map entry, per copier entry — an engine property
heap still held after every document is released (MEASURED_ONLY +13.1 MiB for B1); the PDFRef and PDFName pools fit, the cause is not measured
object-stream output length before compression, and any upper bound on it
browser heap limits, collector timing and array-buffer accounting
safeProductionRecommendation: structural caps on the EXACT terms, checked after load and before copy, with a typed refusal — values are product choices, not memory figures
Merge one source at a time, releasing each, no preloading, with the cumulative output growth checked from each source's plan before its copy
close the load boundary before implementation
objectGraphMemoryConclusion.requiredFollowOn: Load Boundary Sub-Spike — proposed implementation blocker B3
objectGraphMemoryConclusion.adoptedByHuman: 2026-09-15 — memory model PARTIALLY BOUNDABLE, M5 presets DO NOT ADOPT, output ceiling ADOPTED / unchanged
objectGraphMemoryConclusion.historicalNote: At adoption this decision's memory model was UNKNOWN and every preset NOT ADOPTABLE. B2 replaced the UNKNOWN with this conclusion; it did not make any preset adoptable.

loadBoundaryConclusion.outcome: A — CLOSED: hard pre-load boundary proven
hardPreLoadTerms: decoded bytes per object or cross-reference stream, and in total — counted by a bounded inflate that stops at the cap plus one chunk
declared cross-reference entries, from direct /Size or /Index
objects per object stream, from a direct /N, with offsets in order and objects not overlapping
parse work — no more values than raw plus decoded bytes
stillUnknown: heap bytes per parsed object, as B2 left it
which real drawings strict syntax refuses
loadBoundaryConclusion.memoryModel: unchanged — PARTIALLY BOUNDABLE; the load's structure is now bounded before load, its heap bytes are not
loadBoundaryConclusion.historicalNote: H11 was UNKNOWN at adoption; B2 made it PARTIALLY BOUNDABLE and found the load unbounded; B3 was proposed from that finding, accepted by the Human, and closed with this boundary. B3 did not make any preset adoptable.

loadBoundaryDecisions.basis: B3 tested source 2c3f841618514887db0667e0bbc1d72eb32ba42e; evidence-only final 5812c6e5a7ef265ce1f91681dc320549538a06d5; load-boundary gate 98/98 in both runs; exact-head Core CI run 35076759871, attempt 1, success — Core CI is not the research gate

decisions.record: the pre-parse hard boundary is M6's mandatory production load contract. PDFDocument.load() may be called only on input the load boundary PASSes. Dangerous, ambiguous or unsupported load structure is a typed refusal, and fails closed.

decisions.decision: DO NOT ADOPT the research test values as product values
decisions.record: 64 MiB input, 4 MiB decoded bytes per stream, 8 MiB cumulative decoded bytes, 64 decode streams, 100,000 xref entries, 10,000 objects per object stream and depth 64 are research test values, not production defaults. The product policy is blocker B4, which blocks Ready, release and production enablement, not implementation.

B3's evidence holds for the bounded inflate over pako 2.1.0. Production does not rely on a pako that happens to be present transitively: package.json declares pako 2.1.0 as a direct dependency, in the production implementation branch and not in this round. The version contract is bound to the B3 evidence; changing the pako version requires the B3 Load Boundary regression verification again.

decisions.decision: ADOPT a disposable Worker for the M6 processing route
decisions.worker: secondary defence in depth; a Worker alone is NOT a safety boundary

decisions.record: syntax whose safety cannot be proven is not guessed through for compatibility; it fails closed. The user receives a typed refusal whose reason is at least equivalent to 「このPDFは安全に処理できることを確認できなかったため処理しません」. Silent failure is forbidden. The real-drawing compatibility of strict refusal is checked in B4.

the B3 architecture proof is bound to pdf-lib 1.17.1, and M6 production implementation assumes that version's behaviour. On any pdf-lib version change the Load Boundary verification is run again, and M6's safety is not treated as inherited until the decode surface, tokenizer and oracle contracts hold for the new version.

loadBoundaryDecisions.historicalNote: H11 UNKNOWN at adoption (2026-09-14) → B2 PARTIALLY BOUNDABLE (2026-09-15) → B3 discovered and accepted (2026-09-15) → B3 A, hard pre-load boundary proven (2026-09-16) → the Human adopts the production load architecture (2026-09-16) → B4, product load policy, OPEN. This record does not change the B3 research result.

decisions.why: M5 RF-L2 forbade a hard budget containing an UNKNOWN that may materially exceed the ceiling. Reusing M5's presets for a differently shaped operation would be exactly that.
defer: whether the adopted output ceiling shares M5's MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES 268435456 or takes an independently gated M6 value — the research recommends sharing

decisions.question: Thumbnail strategy
candidates: P1 — every page as a Data URL (current)
P2 — windowed rendering
P3 — bounded Blob URLs
P4 — regenerated cache
decisions.measured: P1 retains 88,616 B of UTF-16 payload per A4 page and 538,997 B per A1 sheet (6.2x), 16.9 MiB for 200 A4 pages, 1,727 ms before anything is shown for 100 pages, with no ceiling anywhere. P2 at a 12-page window retains 1.0 MiB against P1's 8.4 MiB on the same source. P3 moves the image payload out of the JS heap: 0.4 MiB of Blob payload, with the URL strings and their JS objects still held.
decisions.recommended: P2 with P3's Blob URLs for the retained window, owned by the run
decisions.adopted: P2 windowed rendering with P3 bounded Blob URLs for the retained window, owned by the run
decisions.basisNote: Character counts and logical UTF-16 payload bytes are EXACT; what a JS engine allocates to hold a string, and the engine's own bookkeeping, are UNKNOWN. An earlier version of this research called characters × 2 'exact retained heap bytes', which it is not, and called P3 '0 B in the JS heap', which overstates it.
decisions.why: The problem with P1 is not speed but that it has no bound: the cost is set by whatever document the user opens. The four terms above are quantities the product chooses and can enforce. No claim is made about total browser heap, which still contains UNKNOWN engine, PDF.js and decoded-image-cache terms.
defer: P4 was not separately measured

decisions.question: Ownership and cancellation
candidates: generalize M5's RunOwnership
a Split/Merge-specific contract
decisions.measured: Two previews started together finish in the order second then first, so the slower first source overwrites the faster second one. There is no run token in the component. 5 exports created 5 object URLs and revoked 0. A PDF.js document opened for a preview is never destroyed.
decisions.recommended: generalize M5's RunOwnership, and extend it with preview-cache and object-URL cleanup on supersede
decisions.adopted: generalize M5's RunOwnership, extended so a superseded run neither publishes nor downloads, revokes its Blob URLs, releases the thumbnail cache and destroys its PDF.js document
decisions.why: The invariant is identical — a superseded run leaves nothing behind — and two incompatible definitions of ownership across tools would be worse than one shared primitive. What M6 adds is that a superseded run must also release retained thumbnails and revoke URLs.

decisions.question: Output naming
candidates: keep extracted_<source>.pdf and merged_document.pdf
derive a self-describing name
decisions.measured: Every merge is named merged_document.pdf, so a second merge overwrites the first in the download folder; an extract says nothing about which pages it contains.
decisions.recommended: self-describing and deterministic: <source>_p1,3,5-8.pdf for Extract, merged_<n>files_<firstSource>.pdf for Merge
decisions.adopted: self-describing and deterministic: <source>_p1,3,5-8.pdf for Extract, merged_<n>files_<firstSource>.pdf for Merge
decisions.why: A download folder is shared state the product writes into; a fixed filename silently destroys the previous result.
defer: length limits for very large selections
